base.preservationRule: V2 raw results, protocol tags, paper, and release assets remain immutable. V3 uses new code, tags, and result directories.

researchQuestion: Under an equal live-evaluation budget, does deterministic two-stage resampling reduce the proportion of provisional optimizer-only Pareto discoveries that fail shared repeated validation compared with one-shot evolutionary search?
validNegativeResults: Two-stage resampling has the same or a higher false Pareto discovery proportion than one-shot search.
Neither arm produces an optimizer-only provisional point.
Neither arm produces a policy that remains nondominated under shared repeated-mean validation.
Two-stage resampling reduces exploration without improving promotion precision.

estimand.experimentalUnit: One fresh policy sample: one normalized policy evaluated once on each fixed training workload using real scheduler rollouts and Pod bindings.
estimand.independentRepetition: One fresh policy-workload replay after scheduler rollout convergence and namespace cleanup.
sampleObjectives: Average p95 scheduler-decision latency across the three training workloads.
Average maximum workload-occupied worker nodes across the three training workloads.
estimand.multiSampleAggregation: Arithmetic mean of the sample-level objective point estimates for each promoted candidate.
estimand.tailMetricLimitation: Each workload replay contains 24 Pods; linearly interpolated p95 depends on the 22nd and 23rd ordered observations and remains sensitive to a few upper-tail samples.
measurementSources: Evaluator submission timestamp immediately before Pod creation request.
Custom scheduler decision annotation immediately before Binding submission.
Kubernetes PodScheduled condition timestamp retained as a separate coarse source.
Evaluator observation timestamp retained as observation lag, not optimizer latency.
safetyMetrics: scheduledCount and completedCount must match Pod count
decision timestamp coverage must be complete
measurement protocol, scheduler interval, polling interval, worker topology, and canonical deployment weights must not drift

commonSearchParameters.policyNormalization: Nonnegative L1 simplex before every live evaluation.

budgetDefinition.exclusions: Post-search shared validation is reported separately and is not charged to either search arm.
budgetDefinition.rolloutTelemetry: Fresh policy samples require deployment update and rollout convergence, but neither the pilot nor official search claims an exact rollout count. A deployment update can be a no-op when the Pod template is unchanged; rollout/update telemetry was not instrumented before this freeze and is therefore not reported as an observed budget.

arms.name: two-stage-resampling
arms.selectionFitness: Arithmetic mean over all fresh samples held by the candidate after deterministic promotion.

promotionRule.timing: After one-shot evaluation of the generation's new offspring and before environmental selection.
promotionRule.eligible: Candidates with exactly one fresh sample that have not previously been promoted.
ordering: lower candidate creation ordinal as deterministic tie-break
promotionRule.action: Collect three additional fresh policy samples for each promoted candidate, recompute objectives from four sample-level estimates, recompute ranks and crowding, then select the next population.
promotionRule.insufficientEligibleAction: Fail the arm and preserve partial artifacts; do not reallocate or silently reduce the fixed budget.

freshEvaluationContract.cachePolicy: Every V3 optimizer, promotion, and baseline sample invokes real workload replay. The V2 phenotype cache must be bypassed.
requiredProvenance: arm, seed, generation, and candidate creation ordinal
sample ordinal and whether it is screening or promotion
fresh evaluation ID and start/finish timestamps
candidate aggregate objective after the sample
cumulative optimizer sample and workload-execution budget
freshEvaluationContract.duplicatePhenotypeRule: Distinct candidate IDs with equal canonical weights still consume independent fresh samples and remain separately traceable. Exact phenotype duplicates are reported.

pilot.workloads: Use all three training workloads so sample aggregation and budget accounting match official semantics.
acceptance: Both arms complete exactly eight optimizer fresh samples and three baseline fresh samples.
The promoted treatment candidate contains exactly three distinct evaluation IDs and sample timestamps.
Candidate aggregate objectives equal the arithmetic mean of retained sample objectives.
No cache hit substitutes for a fresh live replay.
Result and manifest expose exact fresh-policy sample, workload-execution, and Pod budgets plus measured wall time.
No exact scheduler rollout count is claimed without dedicated deployment update and Pod replacement telemetry.
Postflight restores canonical weights, scheduler cadence, clean evaluator namespace, and healthy deployment.

official.estimatedSearchWallTime: Approximately 12 hours 24 minutes for all six arm-seed executions, linearly scaled from the accepted 36 minute 25 second pilot. This is a capacity estimate, not an observed official duration.
official.armOrderDecision: Use the fixed counterbalanced order committed in this protocol. Do not randomize after the pilot; fixed ordering is auditable, balances first-arm position across the two methods as far as three seeds permit, and introduces no result-dependent choice.
runGate: Pilot acceptance is complete and committed.
Implementation, tests, workloads, baselines, analysis schema, and this protocol are committed in a clean tree.
An annotated official V3 protocol tag points exactly at HEAD.
Input checksums, image identity, versions, cluster topology, scheduler cadence, and canonical weights pass preflight.
Output directory is new and manifest starts in running state.
official.failureRule: Any invalid, failed, or interrupted fresh sample fails the arm. Preserve partial outputs and the denominator; do not replace candidates or reduce the budget silently.
official.postflightRule: After every arm and seed, verify deployment health, canonical weights, 250ms measurement cadence during the experiment, clean evaluator namespace, and eventual restoration to the normal 2s idle cadence.

sharedValidation.candidatePoolPerArm: Collect optimizer-only members of each seed's combined provisional point-estimate Pareto front.
sharedValidation.deduplication: Deduplicate exact canonical weight phenotypes within and across seeds while retaining all arm and seed provenance.
capRule: retain pending-best and node-best when distinct
fill remaining slots by descending crowding distance on the pooled unique provisional front
break exact ties by canonical weight key
sharedValidation.commonReferences: Add the three hand-designed V2 baselines and merge exact phenotype duplicates across arms.
sharedValidation.validationBudget: Report separately after finalist selection because the candidate count is outcome-dependent.
sharedValidation.noProvisionalCandidateRule: Report zero promoted finalists and an undefined false discovery proportion for that arm; do not invent a replacement candidate.
sharedValidation.holdout: No V3 holdout is part of this protocol. Any surviving optimizer policy requires a separate committed holdout protocol before a generalization claim.

primaryOutcome.name: falseParetoDiscoveryProportion
primaryOutcome.definition: Number of validated provisional optimizer finalists that do not remain nondominated on the shared repeated-mean point-estimate front divided by the number of provisional optimizer finalists evaluated for that arm.
primaryOutcome.interpretation: Descriptive arm comparison under equal search sample budget; not a hypothesis test with three seeds.

secondaryOutcomes: number and proportion of finalists that remain nondominated
fresh policy samples, workload executions, Pods, and wall time
scheduler deployment update and actual rollout counts are not reported because dedicated telemetry was not added before official freeze
baseline survival and exact duplicate objective points
repeated-mean objective coordinates and 95% Student-t confidence intervals
analysis.paretoLanguage: All fronts derived from sample means are point-estimate Pareto fronts. Dominance is not a statistical significance test.
analysis.mitigationSupportRule: Two-stage mitigation is descriptively supported only if its false Pareto discovery proportion is lower than the one-shot control under the fixed search budget and all safety metrics pass.
analysis.falsificationRule: If the treatment proportion is equal, higher, or undefined while the control is defined, the experiment does not support the mitigation claim.
analysis.optimizerImprovementRule: A new policy improvement may be discussed only if an optimizer finalist remains nondominated against shared repeated baselines. Overlapping marginal confidence intervals still preclude a statistical superiority claim.

implementationAcceptance: The existing V2 one-shot Run path and output remain backward compatible.
Deterministic unit tests prove exact budget accounting for both arms.
Unit tests prove promotion ordering, fresh sample collection, objective aggregation, rank recomputation, and failure on insufficient eligible candidates.
Cluster evaluator tests prove cached V2 evaluation and fresh V3 evaluation are distinct operations.
JSON and CSV outputs include mode, sample count, evaluation IDs, sample objectives, and cumulative budgets.
Pilot runner preserves clean/tag/checksum/preflight/postflight provenance and never labels pilot output as official evidence.

Official launcher enforces the fixed three-seed counterbalanced order, exact per-arm and combined budgets, semantic protocol identity, child manifest acceptance, interruption recovery, and final 2s idle-cadence restoration.
Evaluator-generated Pod names are DNS-1123 labels no longer than 63 characters and pass a warning-free live debug smoke.
resolvedBeforeOfficialFreeze: Implementation-derived top manifest fields are fixed as Git and tag identity, command, common input checksums, explicit execution order, exact combined budget, child manifest and launcher log checksums, execution status, failure detail, and final restoration snapshot.
The accepted pilot measured 36 minutes 25 seconds for 16 optimizer and 6 baseline samples; the official search capacity estimate is approximately 12 hours 24 minutes under linear scaling.
The official protocol tag is protocol-v3-official-search-2026-09-07 and the run name is 2026-09-07-v3-budget-matched-official-search.
The fixed counterbalanced arm order is retained rather than randomized.
